references.text: God remembered Noah and all the wild animals and all the livestock that were with him in the ark. And God caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the water subsided.
The Lord attended to Sarah as he had said, and the Lord did for Sarah as he had promised.
When the Lord saw that Leah was unloved, he opened her womb, but Rachel remained barren.
God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob.
For he remembered his holy word to Abraham, his servant.
But the angel said to him: 'Do not be afraid, Zechariah, for your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall name him John.'

After these days his wife Elizabeth conceived, and she hid herself for five months, saying: 'This is what the Lord has done for me in the days when he looked on me to take away my disgrace among people.'
Verse 6 is the immediate response and confirmation of God's action in verse 22.
It affirms the theological principle that God's listening to prayers leads to concrete action.
It illustrates the theological pattern: Cry for help in distress -> God listens -> Action.
Exodus 2:25 provides the theological premise ('God knew') that is unfolded concretely in Rachel's story.
Complementary events in the same person's life showing God's sovereignty over her entire destiny.
